sections.title: Helpers that format numbers
sections.what: Two small helpers turn numbers into display text. One shows a fraction as a whole percent. The other shows points with a plus or minus sign and one decimal place. Both show a dash when there is no value.
sections.why: Likely reason: the report shows many scores, and these helpers keep them consistent and safe when data is missing.

sections.name: Reads
sections.title: Lists reads without spoilers
sections.what: Shows a titled list of calls. Each entry gives the match, the decision type, the confidence the user gave, whether it was the best call, and its points. If the list is empty, it says none yet.
sections.why: The code comment says a shared Season File must not reveal the answers to golden-moment questions, and cites decision D-045.
sections.watch_out: Adding the name of the best option to this list would reveal answers in every shared report.

sections.name: SeasonFilePage
sections.title: Builds the season report
sections.what: Shows the season report for a signed-in user. It covers the name and date, call counts, best-pick rate, mean read, mean Brier score, the Read Rating, best and worst reads, a calibration chart, a rating history chart, and a print button.
sections.why: Likely reason: a season summary that can be shared and printed, with a closing note that grades are not about results.
sections.watch_out: A new user with no graded calls will see dashes throughout, which is expected but may look like a bug.

summary: Printable season report for a signed-in user, with scores, best and worst reads, and calibration charts.
purpose: Summarises how a user did in the Decision Lab over a season, in a form that can be shared or printed.
why: The report is meant to be shared, so it avoids revealing answers. The closing note says the grades are for bragging rights only.
how: Steps in order: the page checks for a signed-in user and redirects to sign-in if there is none. It loads the season summary. It shows a header with the display name and the date generated. It shows call counts, best-pick rate, mean read, mean Brier score, and the Read Rating, using small formatting helpers. It lists the best and worst reads without naming the best option. It shows a calibration chart and a rating history chart, then a closing note.
inputs: The signed-in user's id, and the season report data returned by the lab service.
outputs: A printable season report page, or a redirect to sign-in.
risks: Revealing the best option in the reads list would spoil golden-moment answers, so that list must stay as it is. Missing values show as dashes, which can look like a bug to a new user. The page relies on several shared components whose behaviour is not in this packet.
debug: If the page keeps redirecting, check the sign-in state. If scores show dashes, check whether the user has any graded calls. If a chart is empty, check the reliability and rating history data from the season report. The print button comes from a separate file that is not shown.
